plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of gain and response lag: first amplitude response calibrates fill rate versus drain before testing decay at zero and linearity at a second amplitude.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises gradually from ~0.38 by ~0.1-0.2 over 10s with visible lag, staying well below 0.85; a flat or falling trace would falsify positive gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Decay at u=0 and direction of gain: comparing zero-input slope to E1 u=0.4 slope separates drain rate from pump gain and tests H1/H2.
experiments.expected_observation: y continues to decay from ~0.28 toward ~0.18-0.22 over 15s with small noise; decay should be as fast or faster than E1 net slope despite lower level if gain is positive, staying far below 0.85.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of gain and linearity at a second higher amplitude and steady-state input needed for target 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises gradually from ~0.04 by ~0.15-0.25 over 10s, staying below ~0.35; flat or continued decay would falsify positive gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Top-end gain and steady-state input for 0.6: a short u=1.0 burst separates linear extrapolation from saturation and tests whether target is reachable without excessive actuation.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with ~2s delay and ~10s lag is right, y holds ~0.25 for ~2s then rises by ~0.10-0.15 to ~0.35-0.40 over 5s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.50; flat or falling would falsify H1.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 and linearity near target, which directly sets controller feedforward and gain.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises gradually from ~0.45 by ~0.08-0.15 to ~0.53-0.60 over 6s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below ~0.65; flat or falling would falsify positive gain near target and imply hold u above 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 and stability in band, which directly sets controller feedforward and whether integral needs to correct up or down.
experiments.expected_observation: y holds near 0.60 +/-0.03 flat or slow rise to ~0.60-0.63 with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.70; fall below 0.55 would imply hold-u >0.6, sharp rise above 0.68 would imply hold-u <0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold 0.6 and near-target gain/linearity: stepping from 0.6 to 0.5 brackets hold-u and measures decay slope at target to set feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: y decays slowly from ~0.63 toward ~0.58-0.62 over 4s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.70; flat or rising would falsify that hold-u is above 0.5 and imply hold-u <=0.5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-level drain rate and lag vs true steady state at 0.5: E7 flat at 0.63-0.64 under u=0.5 could be lag from prior u=0.6 rather than true equilibrium; measuring zero-input decay slope from ~0.64 separates outflow at operating point from pump gain and refines hold-u feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: y breaks within 1-2s then decays from ~0.64 toward ~0.40-0.50 over 10s (~0.015-0.025/s, faster than low-level E2 if outflow rises with level) with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.70; flat or rising would falsify H1/H2.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold 0.6 and near-target gain, which sets controller feedforward; climbing from 0.37 at 0.6 discriminates true equilibrium ~0.6 from transient flat at 0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with ~1-2s delay and ~5-10s lag and hold-u ~0.6 is right, y holds ~0.37 for ~1-2s then rises at ~0.02-0.03/s to ~0.50-0.55 over 7s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below ~0.60; flat or continued decay would falsify H1/H6 and imply hold-u well above 0.6 or loss of gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u=0.6 resumes steady climb from 0.36 after cold-start delay versus true hold-u above 0.6, which directly sets controller feedforward for target 0.6 and delay compensation.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with 2-4s cold-start delay plus 5-10s lag and hold-u ~0.6 is right, y holds/dips near 0.35-0.37 for ~1-2s then rises at ~0.015-0.025/s to ~0.45-0.50 over 7s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below ~0.60; flat or continued decay would falsify H1/H6 and imply hold-u well above 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold 0.6 and near-target climb rate, which directly sets controller feedforward and integral correction.
experiments.expected_observation: y continues climbing from ~0.45 at ~0.012-0.025/s to ~0.52-0.58 over 6s with +/-0.01 noise, entering lower band edge; flat or decay would falsify that u=0.6 equilibrium is >=0.6 and imply hold-u above 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direct delay measurement discriminating longer delay/slower response (C3) from weaker gain (C1), faster outflow (C2), or sensor change (C4), which sets delay compensation and prevents oscillation.
experiments.expected_observation: If longer delay is right, y keeps rising from ~0.20 for ~8-15 s after switch to 0 in response to prior u~1.0 in transit to ~0.30-0.50, then breaks and falls steadily toward ~0.05-0.10 over remainder with +/-0.01 noise; immediate fall with no rise would falsify long delay and favor faster outflow or gain loss.

ledger.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y (positive steady-state gain).
At u=0, y decays toward near-zero due to self-drainage, rate ~0.015/s at low y in E2 and ~0.020-0.027/s at high y in E8, i.e. drain increases with level.
Response has cold-start delay ~2-4s when stepping from u=0 (E3 flat, E9 dip) plus ~5-10s lag; steps between non-zero u respond in ~0.5-1s (E4,E5,E10,E11 show immediate climb).
No large amplitude dead-zone: u=0.4 measurably slows decay vs u=0 and u=0.6 climbs from ~0.36, low-u weakness is delayed onset not threshold.
Steady-state level is approximately linear in u across [0,1].
Steady-state u needed to hold target y=0.6 is ~0.50-0.60, likely ~0.50-0.55, because u=0.5 held 0.63-0.64 flat in E7 and u=0.6 rose 0.60-0.63 in E6 and climbed 0.45 to 0.52 at ~0.012/s in E11.
Sensor noise is small (+/-0.01-0.02) relative to 0.10 band so averaging permits control.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller rise and higher hold-u for 0.6, slower rise at same u.
Change is faster outflow: faster fall at u=0 than E2/E8 ~0.015-0.027/s and lower level held by same u.
Change is slower response / longer delay: command-to-first-response delay grew from ~2-4s to ~8-15s with slower approach, causing overshoot-undershoot oscillation with similar steady-state gain.
Change is sensor offset or noise change: true level dynamics unchanged but readings biased or noisier.
